name: African Nightshade
botanicalName: Solanum retroflexum Dun. (DAFF guideline species); often marketed/consumed interchangeably with S. scabrum within the wider African nightshade (Solanum L. section Solanum) complex
harvestProduct: fresh leaves and tender shoots (ripe black/purple berries also eaten)

evidence.quote: Black nightshade requires optimum temperatures of 20 to 34 ºC. The plant prefers full sunlight, but can grow in partially shaded areas. It is sensitive to frost.
evidence.doc: Solanum retroflexum Dun. — Production guidelines, DAFF, February 2013

evidence.quote: The seedlings are ready for transplanting in four to six weeks when they have 4 to 7 true leaves (10 to15 cm). A spacing of 30 cm by 30 cm is recommended.
evidence.doc: Solanum retroflexum Dun. — Production guidelines, DAFF, February 2013

transplant.notes: Source also allows direct field sowing (rows 15-20cm apart) as an alternative to the nursery/transplant method; the transplant method is the one given a specific final field spacing (30x30cm).

evidence.quote: Production Schedule — Planting [shaded: October, November]; Harvesting [shaded: December]; Marketing [shaded: January, December]
evidence.doc: Solanum retroflexum Dun. — Production guidelines, DAFF, February 2013 (Production Schedule table, read from the shaded cells)

evidence.quote: Harvesting maturity: The crop is ready for harvest 4 weeks from transplanting.
evidence.doc: Solanum retroflexum Dun. — Production guidelines, DAFF, February 2013

daysToHarvestRange.notes: First leaf pick, from transplanting. If sown direct rather than transplanted, adding the source's separately-stated 4-6 week nursery period gives an estimated ~56-70 days from sowing to first harvest, but this total is a derived calculation from two separate figures in the source, not itself a stated number.

harvestPeriodWeeksOrMonths.value: Normally three successive harvests are taken from a planting (WRC/DAFF Production Guidelines for African Leafy Vegetables); the DAFF national schedule shows harvesting/marketing concentrated in Dec-Jan from an Oct-Nov planting.

evidence.quote: After you have harvested the plants for the first time, which you should do by cutting the stem about 5 cm above the soil surface, apply LAN again... Repeat the application of LAN... after the second harvest. Normally, three harvests can be obtained.
evidence.doc: Production Guidelines for African Leafy Vegetables, WRC Report TT 536/12 (Jansen van Rensburg, Van Averbeke, Beletse & Slabbert, 2012, co-published with DAFF)

evidence.quote: A spacing of 30 cm by 30 cm is recommended.
evidence.doc: Solanum retroflexum Dun. — Production guidelines, DAFF, February 2013

rowSpacingRangeCm.notes: Alternative direct-sow method: 'Sow the mixture thinly, either by broadcasting or in rows, 15 to 20 cm apart' — no in-row figure given for that method.

evidence.quote: A spacing of 30 cm by 30 cm is recommended.
evidence.doc: Solanum retroflexum Dun. — Production guidelines, DAFF, February 2013

sowDepthRangeCm.notes: Source says only 'cover with a fine layer of soil' — no numeric depth given.

yield.notes: GAP: no fresh-leaf yield figure (t/ha) found in the DAFF guideline, the WRC/DAFF 'Production Guidelines for African Leafy Vegetables' (TT536/12), or in WebSearch of peer-reviewed SA literature. The DAFF document itself states production levels are unknown ('Statistical data on production levels of black nightshade are not known in South Africa'). A commonly circulated '12 t/ha' figure traces to a non-primary gardening website, not a research/extension source, so it was not used.

ecocrop.row: Solanum nigrum (proxy — S. retroflexum/scabrum not separately listed in ECOCROP)

zoneNotes.lowveld-bushveld: DAFF: 'Black nightshade grows almost anywhere in South Africa, often under marginal conditions' — no zone-specific breakdown given.
zoneNotes.karoo-arid: No zone-specific data; general statement of wide adaptability only.

gaps: No fresh-leaf yield (t/ha) figure found in any consulted source — flagged above.
Only one national sowing/harvest window is published (DAFF schedule); no separate data for winter, all-year or mild-frost climate columns.

No named South African cultivars found; also no ARC-VOPI accession/line names for this species were located in the sources consulted (the ARC's own trial work is referenced only via journal citations we could not access, e.g. Jacoby, Labuschagne & Viljoen 2003 on genetic relationships).

The brief's dual naming 'Solanum retroflexum / scabrum' is only partly resolved: the DAFF guideline documents S. retroflexum specifically. It cites Mwai, Onyango & Abukutsa-Onyango (2007) on taxonomy of the African nightshade (Solanum L. Section Solanum) complex — which includes S. scabrum — but that paper itself was not accessible in this session, so the exact retroflexum/scabrum relationship is not independently verified here.
summary: DAFF's Feb 2013 Solanum retroflexum guideline plus the WRC/DAFF Production Guidelines for African Leafy Vegetables give solid, consistent data for sowing months, first-harvest timing (4 weeks post-transplant) and 30x30cm spacing. The one major gap is yield — no t/ha figure for fresh leaves could be found in any primary or acceptable secondary source, and South Africa has no registered cultivars for this landrace crop.
